spec.title: Welcome to the Engineering Team
spec.subtitle: Your journey to building great software starts here
spec.notes: Welcome to the team! We're excited to have you join us as we continue building products that matter. Over the next few slides, we'll walk you through our engineering principles, the tools we use, and what to expect in your first 90 days. By the end of this session, you'll have a clear picture of how we work and where you fit in. Let's get started.

image.credit: "Area to become Silvertown Quays" by Danny P Robinson, CC BY-SA 2.0

slides.brief: Welcome new software engineers to the team, setting an exciting tone for their onboarding journey.

spec.title: Our Engineering Principles
spec.notes: These four principles guide every decision we make. Quality over speed means we sometimes say no to deadlines that compromise our standards. Continuous learning keeps us growing - expect to present at least once per quarter. Psychological safety is the foundation of our team dynamics; your ideas matter regardless of seniority. Finally, user-first thinking ensures we build things that actually solve real problems.

cards.heading: Quality Over Speed
cards.text: We ship code we're proud of. Code reviews are collaborative, not confrontational. We take time to get it right.

cards.heading: Continuous Learning
cards.text: Every engineer has a learning budget. We encourage conference attendance, online courses, and weekly knowledge-sharing sessions.

cards.heading: Psychological Safety
cards.text: Speak up, ask questions, admit mistakes. No blame culture. Every voice matters in solving hard problems.

cards.heading: User-First Thinking
cards.text: Every feature starts with user needs. We measure success by business impact and customer satisfaction, not shipping velocity.

slides.brief: Highlight core engineering values: quality over speed, continuous learning, psychological safety, and user-first thinking.

spec.title: Tech Stack Overview
spec.notes: This is our production architecture. The React SPA runs as a single-page application served via CDN. Requests flow through a load balancer that handles SSL termination and routes to our Node.js microservices. We use PostgreSQL as the primary data store with Redis in front for caching frequently accessed data. All services are containerized and deployed on AWS using ECS and Kubernetes. Don't worry if this looks complex - you'll get hands-on experience with each layer in your first weeks.
spec.caption: Our full-stack architecture: React frontend communicates via HTTPS through a load balancer to Node.js backend services, backed by PostgreSQL and Redis on AWS.

slides.brief: A clear diagram showing our frontend, backend, data layer, and cloud infrastructure components.

spec.title: Your First 30 Days
spec.notes: Your first month is designed to get you shipping code confidently. Week 1 is all about setup and reading code - we expect this to take 3-5 days. Week 2 you'll pick up a starter bug or small feature with pair programming support. Week 3 introduces you to code reviews - both giving and receiving feedback. By week 4, you'll deploy to production with your buddy watching. Most engineers hit this milestone within 21-25 days. Don't rush - the buddy system ensures you're never alone.

spec.title: Engineering by the Numbers
spec.notes: These numbers represent where we are today - they're not vanity metrics, they reflect our real workflow. We deploy twice per day on average, which means your code reaches users quickly after review. Our 85% test coverage is a floor, not a ceiling - new code is expected to maintain or improve this. We're a team of 10 engineers, which keeps us nimble and lets everyone have genuine ownership. Finally, our PR review turnaround averages under 4 hours - we value fast feedback loops.

spec.title: Tools & Communication
spec.notes: These are the actual tools we use daily - you'll get access on day one. VS Code is our standard editor with pre-configured extensions for linting and formatting. GitHub handles all code review and pull requests - expect to open your first PR in week two. For communication, Slack is our primary hub; we keep meetings minimal and favor async updates. Daily workflow typically starts with a brief Slack standup, followed by focused coding time, and ends with PR reviews. On-call rotation uses PagerDuty - you'll join this after your first month.

spec.title: The 90-Day Roadmap
spec.notes: This roadmap mirrors how we've seen engineers succeed here. The first 30 days focus on learning our patterns and building confidence - you've already seen this in the onboarding timeline. By day 60, you should be picking up features with minimal guidance, though your buddy is still available. Day 90 marks the transition to full ownership: you'll have your own feature area, participate in on-call rotation, and start contributing to technical decisions. Remember, this is a guide not a strict schedule - some engineers accelerate, others need more time, and both are fine.

spec.title: Code Review & Quality Culture
spec.notes: This matrix captures how we balance rigor with pragmatism. On the review side, we expect fast turnaround (under 4 hours) and constructive, specific feedback - code review is a learning conversation, not a gate. For testing, we require unit tests for every PR plus integration tests for API changes, with an 85% coverage floor. Our deployment practices emphasize feature flags for risky changes and canary releases to catch issues before they reach everyone. The guiding principle: shipping fast doesn't mean shipping recklessly - we invest in quality at every stage.

quadrants.heading: Review Standards
quadrants.text: All PRs need at least one approval. Reviewers respond within 4 hours. Focus on logic, architecture, and edge cases—not formatting (linters handle that).

quadrants.heading: Testing Requirements
quadrants.text: Unit tests for every change. Integration tests for API/modifications. Maintain 85% minimum coverage. E2E tests for critical user paths.

quadrants.heading: Review Culture
quadrants.text: Psychological safety first—no shaming. Feedback is collaborative learning. Authors explain their code; reviewers ask questions. Be kind but thorough.

quadrants.heading: Deployment Practices
quadrants.text: Feature flags for risky changes. Canary releases to subset of users. Monitor Datadog post-deploy. Roll back fast if anomalies appear.

spec.title: Welcome Aboard!
spec.subtitle: Let's build something great together
spec.notes: You're now part of a team that values quality, learns continuously, and ships meaningful code. Your buddy will reach out within 24 hours - they're your first point of contact for any question, big or small. The resources on this slide are your home base: bookmark them, use them, and don't hesitate to ask for more. We can't wait to see what you'll build. Welcome to the team!

spec.title: Our Team Culture
spec.notes: This slide captures what makes our team special. Pair programming isn't just encouraged - it's built into how we work. You'll pair with your buddy on your first PR, and many engineers find it their most productive way to solve complex problems. We're genuinely remote-first: your physical location matters less than your ability to collaborate clearly. The weekly sync is our anchor - that's where we share progress, blockers, and ideas. Finally, this is a team that has each other's backs. When something goes wrong in production, we solve it together, not by pointing fingers.
